newsitem.title: UK: Almost half UK managers favour change of government.
newsitem.headline: Almost half UK managers favour change of government.

text.p: With the election just weeks away, almost half of Britain's managers feel the time is ripe for a change of government, according to a survey on Monday.
The Institute of Management (IM) found 49 percent of managers thought that after 18 years, the Conservative Party's rule had lasted long enough.
"Managers seem in the mood for change and will swing behind the party that is most in tune with the business agenda," said IM Director Roger Young.
He said with indications increasingly pointing to a consumer boom and rising inflation, managers were keen to see signs of good economic management from British politicians.

Traditionally viewed as a tax-and-spend' party, bad for economic growth and financial markets, the main opposition Labour Party has changed its image under leader Tony Blair. IM said 43 percent of managers said they would now trust a Labour government to manage Britain's economy competently.
Currently well ahead of the Conservatives in opinion polls, Labour aimed to further woo business managers last week when it launched its business manifesto.
But 60 percent of the 349 managers polled by IM last week still approved the Conservative Party's economic management.
